hints.title: Separate value from angle
hints.body: Substituting x=4 gives f(4)=4sin(4 radians). The outside 4 is an ordinary multiplier; the inside 4 specifies an angle.
hints.recap: Only the trigonometric input needs unit conversion.
hints.pitfall: Changing calculator mode does not change the requested value of x.
hints.pause: Mark which occurrence of 4 is the angle.

recall.reminder: Axis labels and angular units matter; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>π</mi><mtext> radians</mtext></mrow></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>180</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Derive the conversion factor
hints.body: Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow></math> radians <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>180</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow></math> to set up a proportion for the same angle measured in the two units.
hints.recap: Equivalent angular measures must describe the same rotation.
hints.pitfall: Multiplying by the inverse conversion factor changes the direction of conversion.
hints.pause: Use the proportion to find the degree measure needed inside the sine.

recall.reminder: Equivalent angular measures must describe the same rotation.

hints.title: Assemble and check the entry
hints.body: Place the converted angle inside the sine operation, preserving the other multiplication in the original function.
hints.recap: Unit conversion changes the representation of an angle.
hints.pitfall: Check both the sine input and the multiplier outside it against the original substitution.
hints.pause: Build the full calculator expression and compare it with the options.

recall.reminder: Unit conversion changes the representation of an angle.

solution:
The target is f(4)=4sin(4 radians). Since π radians=180∘, the angle 4 radians equals (720π)∘.

A degree-mode calculator must therefore evaluate sin(720π), and the numerical multiplier outside the sine is still 4.

The required entry is 4×sin(180×4÷π): F. Converting the outside 4 would change the function being evaluated.
knowledgePattern: Convert only the trigonometric argument from radians
